button.label: Serial Lookup
button.screentip: Look up one serial in a floating window
button.supertip: Read-only. Shows every field for every ownership record on one serial, without spawning a sheet. The window floats, so you can keep clicking cells - Paste at Selection drops the row into the cell you have selected, as many columns as that sheet wants.

button.label: DCN Lookup
button.screentip: Look up one DCN in a floating window
button.supertip: Read-only. The mirror of Serial Lookup: everything one customer owns, rather than everyone who owns one machine. The list shows the asset - serial, make, model, year, type, status - because the DCN is the same on every row. Same floating window and same Paste at Selection.

button.label: Batch Serials
button.screentip: Look up a column of serial numbers
button.supertip: Read-only. Select a column of serials - one is fine - and it writes an Asset Lookup Results sheet. Failed rows are shaded red: those are unknown, not empty. The results columns paste straight into the operation sheets.

button.label: Batch DCNs
button.screentip: Look up a column of DCNs
button.supertip: Read-only. Same as serial lookup, filtered by Dealer Customer Number. One DCN usually owns many assets, so expect several rows per input value.

menu.label: Build Sheet
menu.supertip: Each sheet is a table: one row per asset, a Result column on the right. A single asset is just one row.

button.label: Add / Update Sheet
button.supertip: Columns: Serial, Make Code, DCN, Ownership Type, Model, Model Year, then the optional fields, then Dealer Make Code. Those first six are lookup columns B:G - drag-select and paste.

button.label: Expire Sheet
button.supertip: Columns: Serial, Make Code, DCN, then Dealer Make Code. The first three are lookup columns B:D - drag-select and paste. Expire REMOVES ownership records; always Validate before you Run.

button.label: Transfer Sheet
button.supertip: Columns: Serial, Make Code, Status, Reason, then Dealer Make Code. The first two are lookup columns B:C. Status is APPROVED or REJECTED; a reason is required to reject. Filter a lookup on OwnershipRequestType = RECEIVED to find the ones waiting on you.

button.label: Validate
button.screentip: Check every row without sending anything
button.supertip: SENDS NOTHING. Works out the operation from the active sheet, checks every row, and writes the outcome to the Result column - green ready, yellow skipped with the reason. On Add / Update it also lists which optional fields are being left out. Always do this first.

button.label: Run
button.screentip: Send every valid row on the active sheet
button.supertip: WRITES TO PRODUCTION CCAT. Works out the operation from the active sheet and confirms once with the row count. Each row gets a colour-coded result: green ok, red failed, yellow skipped. Add / update is idempotent, so failed rows are safe to re-run.

button.label: Settings
button.screentip: Set the proxy URL and function key
button.supertip: Stored per-user in the Windows registry, not inside this add-in file. You can point at a two-column range on a sheet instead of typing them.

button.label: Test Connection
button.screentip: Check the proxy URL, key and network
button.supertip: Sends one harmless read for a serial that does not exist, so it proves the setup without depending on any asset. Says in plain English which part is wrong - no URL, no key, key rejected, wrong address, or nothing answering at all - and what to do about it.

button.label: Logs
button.screentip: Open the lookup and write logs
button.supertip: Two CSVs a month under your own profile. The LOOKUP log records every serial and DCN you search for. The WRITE log records every row Run sends, with the state of the record BEFORE it was touched - that is what answers who expired a record on Tuesday, and what Undo reads to put one back. Kept apart on purpose: a few hundred searches would bury the handful of writes that matter.
